issues.legal_issue: A claims officer determining a secured debt under an estate-vesting claims process may consider other applicable laws when deciding whether the debt is legally and justly due.
material_facts: A creditor filed a claim for amounts said to remain due under a mortgage after the mortgaged estate vested in the State.

The governing claims process required determination of the amount legally and justly due, while its prescribed calculation provisions did not expressly address whether a claim was extinguished or barred under another law.
The debtor contended that the claim had been extinguished under the applicable money-lending law because interest already received exceeded the original loan.
issues.conclusion: The claims officer was entitled to consider the money-lending law in deciding whether any principal was legally and justly due; the prescribed calculation provisions did not prevent consideration of that issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18(1)(a) and 20(1) of the Orissa Estates Abolition Act, 1951, a secured creditor's claim is for the amount legally and justly payable, and the claims officer must initially determine whether any principal is legally and justly due. Section 20(2)(a)–(f) prescribes how principal and interest are calculated, but does not exclude inquiry into whether a claim is true, barred by another law, discharged, or still subsisting. Sections 10 and 11 of the Orissa Money Lenders Act, 1939, were relevant to that inquiry. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.estate_claim_proceeding: A creditor sought determination of a secured debt through a claims process arising from the vesting of an estate.
predicates.claim_requires_legal_entitlement_assessm: The governing claims process required the officer to determine what debt was legally and justly due.
predicates.debtor_raises_external_legal_bar: The debtor contended that another applicable law barred, discharged, or extinguished the claimed debt.

issues.definition: When a secured-debt claim in an estate-vesting proceeding requires an assessment of legal entitlement and the debtor raises an external legal bar, the claims officer may consider other applicable law.

issues.legal_issue: A debt subject to a rule limiting recoverable interest to the original principal is extinguished when the lender has already received interest exceeding that principal.
material_facts: The claim concerned a mortgage loan of £77,500.
The creditor admitted receiving £177,349 18s as interest on that loan, an amount exceeding twice the original principal.
The creditor nevertheless claimed a remaining principal balance and further interest through the estate-vesting claims process.
issues.conclusion: The interest already received had to be appropriated toward satisfaction of the loan, leaving no further amount due under the mortgage.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 10(1) and 10(2) of the Orissa Money Lenders Act, 1939, prevent recovery of pre-suit interest, together with interest already realised, in excess of the original loan and require the excess to be appropriated toward satisfaction of the loan. Section 11 also provides for reopening a transaction and appropriating excess interest toward the loan. Applying those provisions, the Court held that the claim was extinguished. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.applicable_lending_law_limits_interest_t: The applicable lending law limits recoverable interest, including interest already received, to no more than the original principal.
predicates.interest_received_exceeds_original_princ: The lender had already received interest exceeding the original amount lent.

issues.definition: In an estate-vesting claim, when applicable lending law caps recoverable interest at the original principal and the lender has received interest beyond that principal, the remaining debt claim is extinguished.
